lines.text: Let go of a probe above a tunnel straight through the Earth.
The famous answer: forty-two minutes to come out the other side.
That's the textbook version, for an Earth made of one ball of the same rock, all the way through.
At the middle, the probe would be doing nearly eight kilometres a second.
Now use the real Earth, with its dense core. The fall takes thirty-eight minutes and eleven seconds.
Four minutes quicker than the famous answer.
Now pretend the pull never changes at all, the same all the way down.
Two very different pulls, and the answers sit eleven seconds apart.
So why does a pull that never changes land so close? The full video on our channel has the answer. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
